principles: A deduplication must be strictly behaviour-preserving: every execution mode keeps the coverage it had before.
Compare candidates by full execution identity (command, args, shell, cwd, env, timeout, optional), never by script path alone.
When two entries differ only by a selection tag, keep the superset so no mode loses the command.
Prove the result from the runner's own invocation record rather than from an exit code.
drivers: The smoke runs twice on every unfocused validate, so every phase gate that validates pays double for zero extra signal.
validate is on the critical path of REVIEW to TEST and DONE transitions, so wasted time compounds across stories.
The fix must not silently drop the smoke from the fast focus set.

options.name: A: keep focus-tagged object
pros: Deletes the bare string at index 4 and keeps the focus-tagged object, which is a strict superset.
Unfocused runs still execute the smoke once; validate --focus=fast still selects it.
Zero change to arguments, shell handling, cwd, env, timeout or fail-closed behaviour.
cons: The surviving entry is the object form, so the diff looks like the plainer line was the one removed.

options.name: B: keep bare string
pros: Deletes the object at index 12 and keeps the shorter bare string, which reads more simply.
cons: The smoke would silently drop out of the fast focus set, weakening validate --focus=fast.
That is a behaviour change disguised as a cleanup.

options.name: C: leave duplication
pros: Leaving the duplication is the zero-risk option and touches nothing.
cons: The reported waste persists on every validating phase gate.
The duplicate keeps misleading future readers into thinking two distinct checks exist.

rationale: Option A is the only strictly behaviour-preserving edit. Because focus is a selection tag rather than an execution parameter, and unfocused runs execute every configured command, the focus-tagged object covers both the full run and the fast-focused run, while the bare string covers only the full run. Keeping the superset removes the duplicate invocation without reducing coverage in any mode.

preMortem.scenario: The wrong entry is removed and the smoke silently disappears from validate --focus=fast.
preMortem.trigger: Deduping by script path alone and keeping whichever entry appears first.
preMortem.consequence: Focused fast validation loses a guard smoke with no visible failure, so a regression can pass the fast gate.
preMortem.mitigation: Keep the focus-tagged entry and verify selection explicitly under both an unfocused run and validate --focus=fast.

preMortem.scenario: A same-script pair that intentionally differs (different args, timeout, cwd or env) is deleted as a false duplicate.
preMortem.trigger: A dedupe scan that matches on the script filename instead of the whole entry.
preMortem.consequence: A distinct configured check silently stops running and the config loses real coverage.
preMortem.mitigation: Run a full-identity scan that serialises every field, and separately report same-script pairs so differentiated entries are reviewed and preserved.

preMortem.scenario: The exactly-once claim is asserted from a green validate without evidence.
preMortem.trigger: Treating a zero exit code as proof that the duplicate is gone.
preMortem.consequence: A remaining duplicate invocation, or an accidentally dropped invocation, goes unnoticed and the story closes on a false claim.
preMortem.mitigation: Count command results for the script in the validate --json invocation record and require the count to be exactly one.

preMortem.scenario: Hand-editing the JSON corrupts lattice.config.json or reorders unrelated entries.
preMortem.trigger: A careless multi-line edit or a reformatting pass over the whole file.
preMortem.consequence: Config parsing fails or unrelated validate commands change order, breaking validation for every story.
preMortem.mitigation: Delete exactly one line, then re-parse the file with node and diff the normalised command list against the pre-edit list to confirm the only difference is the removed entry.
